findings.evidence: maintenance documentation will be supplied and the operating system will be tested
findings.rationale: Passive voice leaves unspecified which party (Yoggie Corporation or the Web Store developers) is responsible for supplying maintenance documentation and testing the operating system.

findings.evidence: Must use a SQL based database.
findings.rationale: Repeats the requirement to use a SQL-based database already stated in GJ-003 without adding distinct functional scope.

findings.evidence: Other versions may not be 100% compatible. Also other browsers such as Mozilla or Firefox may not be 100% compatible.
findings.rationale: Non-binding phrasing ('may not be 100% compatible') and open-ended examples ('such as') leave expected compatibility behavior for other browser versions and browsers untestable.

findings.evidence: Compatibility is only tested and verified
findings.rationale: Passive voice does not specify which actor or organization is responsible for testing and verifying browser compatibility.

findings.evidence: Compatibility is only tested and verified for Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6 and 7, Netscape Communicator Version 4 and 5.
findings.rationale: Restates the same supported browser list (IE 6 and 7, Netscape Communicator 4 and 5) already specified in GJ-001.

findings.evidence: Shall install online help for users via the web interface
findings.rationale: Omits the subject/actor responsible for installing online help (e.g., the system installer, developers, or administrator).

findings.evidence: Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions for the Administrator.
findings.rationale: Prepositional phrase attachment is ambiguous: 'for the Administrator' could apply only to Installation Instructions or to all three listed documents.

findings.evidence: Shall deliver Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions for the Administrator.
findings.rationale: Omits the subject/actor responsible for delivering the required documentation.

findings.evidence: periodic backups
findings.rationale: 'Periodic' is unquantified and does not define a testable backup frequency.

findings.evidence: periodic backups through a live internet connection
findings.rationale: References recurring backups without specifying the numeric interval/unit, backup destination/retention, or fallback behavior when the live internet connection is unavailable.

findings.evidence: The system shall validate credit cards against fraud.
findings.rationale: Specifies credit card fraud validation without stating what action the system takes when fraud is detected or validation fails.

findings.evidence: all sensitive information
findings.rationale: 'Sensitive information' is undefined and leaves open to interpretation which data elements and endpoints require HTTPS encryption.

findings.evidence: auto detect IP DOS attacks and block IP automatically
findings.rationale: Does not specify the block timeout duration or recovery/unblocking mechanism after an IP is blocked, nor the threshold criteria defining an IP DOS attack.

findings.evidence: The system shall detect consecutive failed login attempts.
findings.rationale: Specifies only detection without defining the resulting system action (e.g., lockout, alert, cooldown) or the threshold count of consecutive failed attempts.

findings.evidence: the system shall validate 'existing' credit card in system after each log in
findings.rationale: Describes validating a returning customer's stored credit card on login without specifying what happens if validation fails or the stored card is expired or invalid.

findings.evidence: too large in size
findings.rationale: 'Too large in size' is subjective and unquantified, providing no testable criterion for when compression is triggered.

findings.evidence: image files that are too large in size
findings.rationale: References a file size threshold without giving the numeric limit and unit (e.g., KB or MB) or the target compressed size/quality.

findings.evidence: faster execution of pages
findings.rationale: 'Faster' is an unquantified comparative term with no baseline or measurable page load/execution time target.

findings.evidence: The system shall validate email address existence.
findings.rationale: Specifies email existence validation without defining how the system responds when an email address does not exist or cannot be verified, or when validation is triggered.

findings.evidence: easy to use
findings.rationale: 'Easy to use' is a subjective usability claim with no measurable acceptance criteria.

findings.evidence: easy to learn
findings.rationale: 'Easy to learn' is a subjective usability claim with no measurable training time or task-completion criteria.

findings.evidence: easy to locate
findings.rationale: 'Easy to locate' is subjective and provides no testable UI placement, sizing, or visibility criteria.

findings.evidence: friend easy to read
findings.rationale: 'Friend[ly]' and 'easy to read' are subjective, unquantified adjectives with no measurable readability or style standards.

findings.evidence: consistent symbols and colors for clear notifications
findings.rationale: 'Consistent' and 'clear' are subjective and unquantified without a defined icon/color convention or notification standard.

findings.evidence: interchangeable plugins
findings.rationale: 'Interchangeable' is unquantified and lacks testable criteria specifying which capabilities are pluggable or what plugin interface standard is required.

findings.evidence: easily updatable
findings.rationale: 'Easily updatable' is a subjective maintainability term with no measurable time, effort, or procedural threshold.

findings.evidence: the site
findings.rationale: Refers to the product as 'the site' instead of the established name 'Web Store' (and alongside 'The system' in the same sentence), introducing terminology drift.

findings.evidence: easy to upgrade
findings.rationale: 'Easy to upgrade' is a subjective maintainability claim with no measurable upgrade effort, downtime, or verification criteria.

findings.evidence: extremely portable
findings.rationale: 'Extremely portable' is subjective and unquantified, lacking measurable portability criteria.

findings.evidence: easy to migrate or backed up
findings.rationale: 'Easy' is subjective and unquantified, providing no testable threshold for migration or backup effort or duration.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding modal 'should' instead of 'shall', making it unclear whether debug mode support is mandatory or optional.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding modal 'should' instead of 'shall', making it unclear whether running test credit card transactions is mandatory or optional.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding modal 'should' instead of 'shall', making it unclear whether running test shipping orders is mandatory or optional.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding modal 'should' instead of 'shall', making it unclear whether creating a test environment is mandatory or optional.

findings.evidence: weborder system
findings.rationale: Introduces the undefined product label 'weborder system' instead of the established name 'Web Store'.

findings.evidence: The system hardware shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection.
findings.rationale: Passive voice does not identify who or which system component performs the fixing and patching.

findings.evidence: The system hardware shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection.
findings.rationale: Requiring the system hardware to be fixed and patched remotely conflicts with GJ-010, which assumes Yoggie will freeze the baseline of the USB system after delivery.

findings.evidence: coordinate on future enhancement and features with our organization
findings.rationale: 'Coordinate on future enhancement and features' has no measurable obligations, schedule, or acceptance criteria, and 'our organization' is unnamed.

findings.evidence: OS: Apache web server
findings.rationale: Lists 'Apache web server' as the operating system (omitting Slackware Linux 2.6), conflicting with GJ-002 which specifies Slackware Linux 2.6 as the operating system and Apache Web Server as the web server.
